author: jtraglia
content:
Hi devs, we are considering restricting which EIPs (features) may add/modify tests in the specifications. The [current proposal](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/5618) is:
* anyone can add specs for their EIP into consensus-specs
* only EIPs which have been CFI'd or SFI'd may add/modify tests
We're looking to make this change because modifying the testing infrastructure for every EIP is a bit invasive and just requires a lot more attention to detail; specs are mostly self-contained which is easier. The downside of this is that it _could_ make it more difficult to jump from PFI to CFI without tests. But EIP champions could create/generate tests in their own forks, outside of `ethereum/consensus-specs`. Curious to hear what y'all think. cc <@586161934425128960> <@845691100072509460> <@755590043632140352> <@654267572107083777> <@486501030046203915> <@402080271563751435> and others.

author: taulepton_
content:
I think this is a reasonable trade-off if capacity is saturated (which I have no doubt it is 😅). The specs themselves are the primary medium we collaborate on, so I see value in using the consensus-specs repo for that (again, if capacity allows). I've also found that the consensus-specs architecture is conducive to extension, which is nice. 

A fork could certainly work, but I also wonder whether we can create a "cookie-cutter" repo template that lets an eip maintainer import the specs from a versioned release and specify tests in a standardised way. I don't have enough context to have a strong opinion here, but I wanted to surface the idea.
